title: Finitely many sections of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$ lie in one $E_X$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $\Qlb$ be an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $X$ be a scheme. Use the small pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site] and a universe containing the site and the small indexing diagrams. Let $V$ be a quasi-compact object, with quasi-compactness as in [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Write $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ and $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$ for the coefficient sheaves of [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] and [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring], using the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed].

1. For every small filtered diagram of sheaves of sets (or abelian groups) $(\mathcal F_\alpha)$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha(V)\longrightarrow(\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha)(V)$$
is injective. It is bijective if $V$ is also quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], or if every transition map is injective on sections over every object of the site. Colimits on the right are sheaf colimits and those on the left are colimits of sets (respectively abelian groups), as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
2. Without any quasi-separatedness assumption on $V$, the maps $E_X(V)\to\QbarX(V)$ are injective and
$$\QbarX(V)=\bigcup_{\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb,\ [E:\mathbf Q_\ell]<\infty} E_X(V).$$
Every finite set of elements of $\QbarX(V)$ lies in one $E_X(V)$. For a finite family of matrices, each with finitely many rows and columns and entries in $\QbarX(V)$, all entries lie in one such $E_X(V)$.

proof.text: First work with sheaves of sets. Put $P(U)=\varinjlim_\alpha\mathcal F_\alpha(U)$. The sectionwise-colimit theorem makes $P$ the presheaf colimit. By the sheafification adjunction, $P^\#$ is the sheaf colimit: a map from $P^\#$ to any sheaf is exactly a compatible family of maps from the $\mathcal F_\alpha$. Concretely $P(U)$ is the disjoint union of the $\mathcal F_\alpha(U)$ modulo eventual equality. Filteredness makes the relation 'equal after mapping to a common stage' transitive: take a common cocone on the finitely many stages and arrows witnessing two successive equalities. Thus each element has a stage representative and equality of representatives is witnessed at a common stage. This also explains every use of a common stage below, for a filtered category as well as for a directed poset. In Lean, presheaf_colimit constructs this comparison from Sheaf.isColimitSheafifyCocone and identifies its legs. The proved larger-universe set-sheafification theorem supplies local injectivity and local surjectivity for the value universe max(u+1,v). Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit supplies representatives and eventual equality, including the same-stage version that equalizes parallel arrows.

proof.text: First suppose T is affine. Extract a pro-etale precoverage family inside the given covering sieve and its QuasiCompactCover certificate. Apply QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom to obtain a finite affine refinement. Its arrows have affine source and affine target, so this finite family is itself quasi-compact, and hence remains a pro-etale cover. For general quasi-compact T, choose a finite subcover of its affine open cover, pull the given covering sieve back to each affine member, and apply the affine case. Compose these finitely many finite families. GrothendieckTopology.bindOfArrows proves that the composite family covers T; every composite lies in the original sieve by downward closure. This is implemented by finite_affine_cover_of_affine and finite_affine_cover. No quasi-separatedness of T is used.

source.place: Tag 0989 (definition-fpqc-covering), applied on a finite affine open cover of T

proof.text: The local injectivity of the presheaf-to-sheaf colimit comparison gives a covering equalizer sieve for any two same-stage sections with equal images. On each member, Types.FilteredColimit.isColimit_eq_iff′ gives one later arrow making the restrictions equal, including equalization of parallel arrows. Apply the finite affine refinement of step 2. A finite cocone on all the witnesses and the arrows out of the original index produces one common arrow. Naturality and separatedness of the sheaf at that stage prove equality on T. This is eventual_equality. Finally represent any two elements in the section colimit at one common stage; the canonical leg equations and eventual equality prove injectivity of colimit.desc.

If $V$ is quasi-separated and $A,B\to V$ are affine objects of a covering, then $A\times_V B$ is quasi-compact. It is the pullback of the quasi-compact diagonal $V\to V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}V$ along $A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}B\to V\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}V$. Its projection to $A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}B$ is quasi-compact by base change. The latter is affine by the affine-spectrum fibre-product theorem, so its whole inverse image is quasi-compact by the definition of a quasi-compact morphism. Now let $s\in P^\#(V)$. Choose local representatives and refine to a finite affine cover as in step 2. Move their finitely many stages to a common stage. On each pairwise overlap their images in $P^\#$ agree; step 3 and the just-proved quasi-compactness give equality at a later stage. Take a common cocone on the finitely many overlap witnesses. The resulting sections are compatible and glue in that stage sheaf to a section on $V$ mapping to $s$. Together with step 3 this proves the quasi-separated case of clause (1). The Lean proof section_representative transports the scheme pullback compactness across PreservesPullback.iso for the forgetful functor X.ProEt to schemes. finite_common_arrow makes all overlap equalities hold after a single arrow. Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff_pullbacks glues the resulting family, and separatedness of the colimit sheaf identifies its image with the original section.

source.place: Tag 0738 (lemma-directed-colimits-sections), proof of (4); geometry: schemes.tex Tags 01KK (definition-separated), items (2) and (4), 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes)

proof.text: Instead assume all transition maps are injective on every object. Then $\mathcal F_\alpha(U)\to P(U)$ is injective for every $U$: if $s,t\in\mathcal F_\alpha(U)$ have the same image, there are arrows $f,g:\alpha\to\beta$ with $\mathcal F(f)(s)=\mathcal F(g)(t)$. Filteredness gives $h:\beta\to\gamma$ with $hf=hg$. Applying $\mathcal F(h)$ and using injectivity of $\mathcal F(hf)$ gives $s=t$. If two sections of $\mathcal F_\alpha(U)$ have equal images in $P^\#(U)$, the local equality description of sheafification and this sectionwise injectivity make them locally equal in $\mathcal F_\alpha$, hence equal by its sheaf condition. Thus $\mathcal F_\alpha(U)\to P^\#(U)$ is injective for every $U$, with no compactness hypothesis. For $s\in P^\#(V)$ use local representatives and a finite refinement as in step 2, and move the representatives to one stage $\alpha$. On any overlap they agree in $P^\#$, so they agree already in $\mathcal F_\alpha$ by the preceding injectivity, even when that overlap is not quasi-compact. They glue to a representative on $V$. This proves the injective-transition case of clause (1) without quasi-separatedness. In Lean, stage_injective proves this on every object from local_equality and separatedness. section_representative uses it on the overlaps before any compactness argument; the identity arrow already makes the two restrictions agree at their common stage. It then uses the same finite-stage gluing as in step 4.

For abelian sheaves, forgetting to sets preserves filtered colimits and sheafification. The sheafification adjunction and its fully faithful right adjoint therefore show that the induced forgetful functor on sheaves preserves the given filtered colimit. Apply the set comparison of steps 3--5 to the underlying set diagram. The canonical comparison from the colimit of underlying groups to the underlying group colimit is an isomorphism. Its composite with the underlying abelian section comparison is the set section comparison, by colimit.post_desc. Bijectivity of this first comparison transfers injectivity and conditional bijectivity to the abelian comparison. Universe shrinking supplies filtered-colimit preservation at the site-cover and diagram sizes separately. This step is now proved in Lean from the set comparison, which is now completely proved.

For each finite field E, the condensed inclusion into the algebraic closure is injective on every profinite test object: evaluate equality of continuous functions pointwise and use injectivity of the subfield inclusion. Hence this sheaf map is monic. The existing constructed point pullback preserves finite limits by Mathlib sheafPullbackConstruction, since the test-object functor is representably flat. Scheme inverse image also preserves finite limits, so their composite p_X^* preserves this monomorphism. Sheaf evaluation is left exact, so the coefficient inclusion E_X(U) to Qbar_X(U) is injective for every U. The transition E_X(U) to F_X(U) is injective because its composite with F_X(U) to Qbar_X(U) is this injective inclusion. This is proved in the private helper coefficient_section_injective and the local htrans proof; no separate exactness specification theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 00X6 (proposition-get-morphism); coefficient maps and test functor as in the current blueprint proof, clause (2)

proof.text: Use the finite-subextension abelian colimit already proved in the source library as AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isColimitPadicAlgClRingObjCocone, the underlying abelian comparison in sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x. Apply the abelian theorem of step 6 at the small finite-field index category, using step 7 to supply injective transitions. Its surjective section comparison and the jointly-surjective colimit legs of the section groups give a finite-field representative of every section of Qbar_X(V). The leg equations colimit.ι_desc identify these representatives with exactly the prescribed coefficient inclusions. Together with step 7 this proves the injectivity and union assertions. This uses the existing abelian colimit directly, with no completed integral, rationalization, or ring-sheaf comparison required.

source.place: Proof, clause (2), with the injective-transition case of Stacks Tag 0738(3) in place of the invalid unrestricted quasi-compact assertion

proof.text: Prove finite-set descent by induction. The empty set uses any finite subextension, available because the base field is finite over itself. For insertion of s, choose a representing field E for s, a field F for the old finite set, and a common upper bound G. The identity padicSubfieldRingObjMap_comp_toPadicAlgCl proves range monotonicity, so both parts lie in G_X(V). For a finite family of finite matrices the dependent sum of all row-column positions is finite; apply finite-set descent to the range of its entry function. Empty families and empty dimensions are included. This argument is complete Lean.

I checked the doubled convergent-sequence counterexample myself: V = two copies of Spec(eventually constant F_2-sequences) glued along N is quasi-compact but not quasi-separated; the finite gluings V_S are etale over V with sheaf colimit h_V, and no V_S has a section over V. The corrected clause (1) matches Stacks sites.tex 0738(2)-(4). Clause (2) is unchanged and is all that downstream nodes use. Steps: 1 (sectionwise colimit, sheafification adjunction, filtered cocone) and 2 (finite affine refinement from the 0989 condition) are elementary. 3 is 0738(2) via 00WK. 4 handles the quasi-separated case: A x_V B is the base change of the diagonal over affine A x_Z B, using 01K5 and 01I4. 5 handles injective transitions without quasi-compact overlaps, with the parallel arrows equalized. 6 covers abelian groups and rings through the underlying-set sheafification. 7 shows the coefficient maps stay injective: p^* is exact by the left-exact inverse-image lemma (test functor preserves finite limits and coverings), pi_X^* by the scheme inverse-image theorem, and Gamma(U,-) is left exact. 8 uses only the finite-subextension ring-sheaf colimit clause of sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x. 9 is directedness. The coefficient ring is the finite-subextension condensed ring, consistent with the cited definitions. No duplicates: the existing site nodes need finite-index coverings, and the qcqs pro-etale section-calculus node needs quasi-separated V.
